title: Aeolus and the Bag of Winds (on the sea kit)
part: The sea kit on the floating island of the winds
hypothesis: Aeolus's gift and his curse read as a king on an island in open water, and the ship as a ship at sea, if the water is a stepped brick ocean that moves, the island is land standing out of it (Homer X.3-4: a floating island, a wall of unbroken bronze about it), and the light turns from a clear calm under the gift to an overcast rising wind under the curse.
variable: look.sea on K2 (day: swell 0.5, wind 0.35, the sea three plates under the island's land and the ship lowered with it; the island piece's baked water taken out and its baseplate stood on a skirt of 1x4 bricks with a pearl-gold wall on its far sides) and K5 (swell 0.62, wind 0.65, clouds 0.7, storm 0.12, a grey sky). Same sheet, voice, cut and shot plan (re-solved: 6 of 6 legal).

faults: a checkerboard floor of baked water; the island a patch in it; no weather between the two lines

metrics_after.clip: CLIP OD-B10-S01 visible 0.0 s in 0 intervals (tools/metis/clip.js, camera replay)

checks.test: no one runs through anything: Odysseus's feet on the bow's deck as she heaves and rolls; Aeolus on his land, the sea below his feet
checks.note: clip.js: 0 intervals; the ship's rig (the sheet's riders) carries Odysseus with the kit's heave, pitch and roll; the sea lowered 3 plates so the swell never reaches the island's top (in the first dev pass it stood to Aeolus's shins)

checks.test: the island reads as land in open water
checks.note: the stepped ocean to the horizon on every side; the island's baseplate on a grey brick skirt to the sea floor; a gold-brick wall on the two sides away from the ship (not between the lens and Aeolus)

checks.test: the weather turns between the gift and the curse
checks.note: the swell, wind and foam rise and grey plate clouds come over the cut at 16.7 s; the sky's grey is slight in the closes, which are mostly faces

result: Published as take 2. The ship heaves on a stepped brick sea beside a walled island, Odysseus stands on her bow through the gift and the curse, and the sea rises under the curse. Loose: the closes (most of the scene) are faces against sky and sail, so the weather's turn is seen mainly in the water behind them; the sail is the baked translucent one; the bag's handoff is across the water as staged (the bag stays in Aeolus's hand).
